subtitle: A guild at the forest entrance

body: Etrian Odyssey is Atlus and Lancarse's Nintendo DS dungeon role-playing game about a player-created guild exploring the Yggdrasil Labyrinth. A first-person view shows the route ahead while the touchscreen holds a map that the player must draw and annotate. The party advances in measured steps, returning to town to rest, prepare and develop its members. The approach gives exploration a patient, practical character. Progress means understanding a place well enough to record it, then judging whether the party can safely push beyond the point already reached.

The stylus marks paths and places symbols on a grid as the party discovers the labyrinth. A useful note can identify a door, a resource or a route that will matter when supplies are lower. The map is therefore something the player makes alongside the characters' improvement. An inaccurate drawing can complicate the return journey, while a careful one supports the next expedition. Etrian Odyssey uses the DS's second screen to restore a personal record of discovery, putting the familiar role-playing map back into the explorer's hands.

Powerful wandering FOEs occupy the labyrinth alongside ordinary encounters. Their movements advance with the party's actions, making a corridor's layout important before combat begins. Several can converge if the party remains in a dangerous position. Building a five-person team from different classes gives the player choices in preparation, but those choices do not make every visible threat a sensible target. The party's abilities and the map work together: understanding where an enemy can move may preserve the expedition more effectively than winning another difficult fight.
